name: sacrifice
quote: Please, I want you to have this.
description: Giving away something you value to a person or group you perceive as wanting it, but not expecting it, and without your expectation of repayment of any kind.

variations.name: material sacrifice
variations.description: Giving away something of monetary or sentimental value to another who you think needs it more than you do without expectation of repayment of any kind.

variations.name: social sacrifice
variations.description: Giving away a social asset to another who you think needs it more than you do without expectation of repayment of any kind.
examples: spending your weekend volunteering rather than on the beach

variations.name: existential sacrifice
variations.description: Giving your life to protect a person or group without expectation of repayment of any kind.

commentaries.quote: When ancient people sacrificed animals to their gods, it was enough for them to imagine that the gods actually wanted the animal spirits. Giving away the animal may have hurt some, but they gained a sense of control, however illusory. The real sacrifice, of course, belonged to the animals.

In a world that often values self-interest and personal gain, it’s important to remember the power of sacrifice and selflessness. Sacrifice is the ultimate act of love and compassion, demonstrating our willingness to put others before ourselves. Whether it’s giving up our time, resources, or even our own desires, sacrifice has the ability to inspire and encourage those around us.
We make small and large sacrifices when we try to adhere to the ideals of key identities and heroes. What would a good friend do? What kind of parent do I want to be? What would my spiritual hero do?

A sacrifice is not expected. It's got to hurt at least a little and it cannot be for show. It honestly does not expect repayment, even in bragging rights. The recipient should need the sacrifice in some way. The payoff is in a sense of self-worth and perhaps a quiet hope that it will increase a social bank account with someone, whether in this life or the next. Is it a sacrifice for a rich person to give a car to his kid as a birthday gift? No. Is it a sacrifice for an average person to give his car to a stranger who needs it to get to work? Yes.

conditions: Giving away something you value to a person or group you perceive as wanting it, but not expecting it, and without your expectation of repayment of any kind.
